peer_coordination.read_only_recon_result: The existing wiki section 'Compiled Update - 2026-08-21' covers the vacuous-pass campaign on TEST SUITES: tests that DO NOT RUN (Shape A fixture-suite-with-no-__main__, Shape B self-runner-with-no-collectable-test). Its meta-lesson is 'a guard must model the collector it reasons about, or it becomes the defect class it polices' - the collectability gate needed FIVE false-positive repairs, all UNDER-counting what pytest collects. The enforcement chain is: (1) pre-commit lint on changed files, blocking for Shape B and advisory for Shape A; (2) pytest.ini filterwarnings error on PytestReturnNotNoneWarning; (3) per-clone install_git_hooks.sh, which is the known gap - a fresh worktree is unprotected until it runs. Deliberately a LINT AT AUTHORING TIME rather than a pytest_collection_modifyitems floor, because a floor runs inside pytest where a mis-fire breaks every invocation and cannot express 'self-runner ON PURPOSE'. THIS SESSION'S FINDING IS ADDITIVE, NOT OVERLAPPING: it is a THIRD shape - a gate that DOES run and DOES pass, but can be passed by WEAKENING THE COMPUTATION UNDER TEST. Evidence from three independent dived sources: intake-1222's entire correctness gate is one torch.allclose(atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-3) line and its flagship 12.1x came mostly from a TF32->BF16 downgrade that gate admits by construction; intake-1219 ships a self-labelled 'Level 1' anti-cache defence whose perturbation is applied ONCE BEFORE the timed loop and, for all non-fp32/fp64 dtypes, is an order-reversal that is an IDENTITY for order-insensitive kernels; and intake-668 + intake-1220 independently argue KernelBench coverage manufactures an 'illusion of solvedness'. The proposed pairing follows the existing doctrine exactly - an authoring-time / eval-contract precision-equivalence check beside the collectability check, NOT a runtime floor.

evidence_now_five_independent_sources_al: intake-1222 (KernelPro): the ENTIRE correctness gate is one line - torch.allclose(out, ref, atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-3) - and Appendix G.1 states the decisive 4.11x->11.49x jump on its flagship task came from epilogue fusion PLUS a TF32->BF16 tensor-core switch, with the authors conceding 'the precision switch supplies most of the magnitude'. A TF32->BF16 downgrade passes atol=1e-2 BY CONSTRUCTION.

intake-1219 (Hawkeye repo): a self-labelled 'ANTI-CACHE (Level 1)' defence whose input perturbation is applied ONCE BEFORE the timed loop and, for every dtype other than fp32/fp64, is an element-order REVERSAL - an involution that is an IDENTITY for order-insensitive kernels, making the check vacuous for those leaves.

intake-1224 (BackendBench): gate is assert_close at atol=rtol=1e-2 on a bfloat16 suite, so an fp32->bf16 downgrade is not even EXPRESSIBLE; and eval.allclose accepts tolerance args but DROPS THEM, so the tolerance cannot be tightened from the call site.

intake-1227 (KernelGenBench): a genuinely ENGINEERED gate (combinatorial all-cases-must-pass, adaptive tolerance, three-tier anti-hack) that STILL plausibly admits the downgrade on large-K GEMM, because atol = 1e-4 x D_reduce grows LINEARLY with reduction depth and at its own BLAS shape reaches ~0.53, dominating rtol*|ref| by ~3 orders of magnitude. Its anti-hack tiers are ORTHOGONAL - they test whether the kernel RAN, never at what WIDTH it computed.

intake-1236 (QiMeng-Kernel): the released RL environment ships CALL_LIBRARY ('replace the selected operator with library functions') and SOTA_TRITON_API action tags, NEITHER disclosed in the paper - an agent that can satisfy a Torch-Eager-relative speedup reward by calling the vendor library instead of generating a kernel.
